title: The Stabilizer Formalism
summary: Describe a code by commuting Pauli operators and read the syndrome from commutation with them.
objectives: Decide whether two Pauli strings commute or anticommute.
Compute the syndrome of a Pauli error for any list of stabilizer generators.
Build the syndrome table of the bit-flip code and identify the errors it cannot detect.
Find logical operators: Pauli strings that commute with every generator but are not in the stabilizer group.
mission: Pauli strings are written as text, for example "ZZI". Write commutes(a, b), which returns True when two Pauli strings of equal length commute. Write syndrome(error, stabilizers), which returns a tuple with one bit per generator: 0 if the error commutes with it, 1 if it anticommutes. Store in table the syndrome of each of the nine single-qubit errors ("XII", "YII", "ZII", "IXI", …) for the bit-flip code generators in STABILIZERS. Finally set logical_X and logical_Z to Pauli strings that act as X and Z on the encoded qubit.

prediction.question: For the generators Z₁Z₂ and Z₂Z₃, which single-qubit errors have syndrome (0, 0), so that the code cannot detect them?
options: None: every single-qubit error changes at least one eigenvalue
Z on any of the three qubits
prediction.explanation: Z commutes with Z₁Z₂ and Z₂Z₃, so a Z error leaves both eigenvalues at +1. It is not a stabilizer element either, so it changes the encoded state: Z on any qubit acts as the logical Z. Y anticommutes with Z exactly as X does, so Y on the middle qubit gives syndrome (1, 1).

hints: Compare the two strings position by position. Two single-qubit Paulis anticommute when both are different from I and they are different from each other (X and Z, X and Y, Y and Z). The strings commute when the number of anticommuting positions is even.

syndrome(error, stabilizers) is a tuple with one entry per generator g: 0 if commutes(error, g), 1 otherwise. Build the nine errors by placing X, Y or Z at one position of "III", and fill table with a dictionary comprehension over them.

A logical operator commutes with ZZI and IZZ but is not a product of them. XXX flips every qubit, so it maps |000⟩ to |111⟩. For the logical Z, a single Z on one qubit works, and it must anticommute with logical_X.
